description:
## What

Track the human decisions required to declare and ship a PKIX workspace 1.0 release. The architectural decisions are settled (this session and earlier sessions cleared the design frontier); what remains is **scope, disposition, and release mechanics** — all of which are maintainer calls, not autonomous-eligible.

The autonomous loop can drive everything 1.0 needs **after** these decisions land. Pre-this-bead, AGENTS.md explicitly says "no work is gated by a version milestone" (prelaunch framing). This bead changes that: 1.0 becomes the milestone, and the children name what 1.0 includes.

## Children (decision beads + execution beads)

Five human-decision children + two autonomous-execution children + a note about the manual publish step:

- **.1 — Scope definition** (HUMAN; biggest call; gates everything else)
- **.2 — Skeleton/stub crate disposition** (HUMAN; ~6 per-crate ship-or-hold calls)
- **.3 — API stability final pass** (HUMAN review; may surface 0-5 small decisions)
- **.4 — Test acceptance criteria** (HUMAN; PKITS + limbo pass-rate bars)
- **.5 — Release mechanics** (HUMAN/AUTO mix; tag scheme, CHANGELOG style, publish order)
- **.6 — Per-crate `# Limitations` rustdoc audit** (AUTONOMOUS, blocks on .1+.2)
- **.7 — CHANGELOG roll-up + workspace-level release notes** (AUTONOMOUS, blocks on .6)

**Not beaded — Mark's hands:** `cargo publish` cascade. Per AGENTS.md "Git" section and analogous to upstream-write rules, publishing to crates.io is a maintainer action requiring explicit per-action authorization. Agent prepares everything up to but not including the publish step.

## Why narrow scope is the recommended starting point

(From in-session discussion, recording for future reference)

Three scope candidates:

- **(narrow)** ~11 crates: pkix-path, pkix-revocation, pkix-chain, pkix-path-builder, pkix-truststore, pkix-identity, pkix-profiles, pkix-profiles-cabf, pkix-lint, pkix-lint-cabf, pkix-revocation-http. Adjacent and skeleton crates stay at independent 0.x cadence post-1.0.
- **(wide)** Add: pkix-aia, pkix-aia-http, pkix-policy-zlint, pkix-policy-pkilint, pkix-zlint-bridge, pkix-pkilint-bridge. ~17 crates. Requires AiaFetcher + adapter cascade to land.
- **(very wide)** Add: DANE, fully-implemented AC. ~22+ crates. 2-3 months.

The narrow read is most defensible because it matches the AGENTS.md driving goal verbatim ("RFC 5280 X.509 for Rust, done right from the start") without padding it with adjacent ecosystem work. The adjacent crates are real value but they're *additive*, not part of the 1.0 promise.

## Realistic timelines

| Scope | Human time | Autonomous time | Total |
|---|---|---|---|
| narrow | ~3-4h spread over 1-2 weeks | ~3-5 days loop | 1-2 weeks |
| wide | ~4-6h over 3-4 weeks | ~2-3 weeks loop | 3-4 weeks |
| very wide | ~8h+ over months | ~2-3 months loop | 2-3 months |

## Acceptance

- [ ] All five HUMAN-decision children resolved
- [ ] Two AUTONOMOUS-execution children completed by loop
- [ ] CHANGELOGs reflect 1.0 release
- [ ] Per-crate `# Limitations` rustdoc sections audited for accuracy
- [ ] Mark executes `cargo publish` cascade (not in this bead's scope; manual)
- [ ] AGENTS.md "Status" section updated to reflect 1.0 as a shipped milestone (no longer "no work gated by version milestone" for the 1.0-included crates)
- [ ] Workspace tag `v1.0.0` (or per-crate tags `pkix-path-1.0.0` etc. per .5 decision)

## Out of scope

- Implementation work on any 1.0-included crate (tracked in their own beads)
- Post-1.0 roadmap for the adjacent ecosystem (separate beads, separate cadences)
- Publishing to crates.io (Mark's manual action)

## Cross-references

- AGENTS.md "Status" section (currently says "no work gated by version milestone" — this bead changes that)
- AGENTS.md driving goal ("RFC 5280 X.509 for Rust, done right from the start")
- All currently-open beads: this roadmap implicitly schedules them as in-1.0 or post-1.0 per .1 scope
notes:
[2026-05-13 all 5 human-decision children resolved]

All scope/disposition/audit decisions landed today:

- .1 scope: narrow (12 crates incl. pkix-aia per Verifier-generic decision)
- .2 skeleton disposition: all 6 hold at 0.x
- .3 API stability pass: Verifier 3-generic w/ NoAiaFetcher default; serde opt-in; re-exports unchanged; MSRV 1.73; no naming items; derive audit folded into .6
- .4 test acceptance: PKITS 100% except documented divergences; limbo 25/26 residuals accepted; PKIX-lwr9.4 is 1.0-blocker; baseline docs reviewed
- .5 release mechanics: per-crate tags + per-crate CHANGELOGs; topological publish order; dry-runs mandatory; Mark runs publish

Now unblocked (autonomous-eligible):
- .6 Limitations audit (was blocked on .1+.2)
- .7 CHANGELOG roll-up (blocks on .6)

1.0 blocker labeled beads (5 total):
- PKIX-zkjb.2 AiaError type
- PKIX-zkjb.3 AiaFetcher trait
- PKIX-zkjb.4 NoAiaFetcher default
- PKIX-zkjb.9 Verifier 3-generic API freeze
- PKIX-lwr9.4 bettertls tc60 path-builder bug fix

Plus autonomous-execution work:
- .6 Limitations rustdoc audit (per crate, 12 crates)
- .7 CHANGELOG roll-up + workspace release notes

Estimated 1.0 timeline: ~1-2 weeks of autonomous loop + Mark's review at the end + manual publish.
